---
title: "Installation"
---

## Requirements

- Python 3.12, pinned in `.python-version` and enforced by `pyproject.toml`
- [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) for dependency management
- About 4 GB of disk space for the environment. The data need far more (see [Data](data.qmd)).

## Install

Install uv if it is missing:

```bash
# Windows PowerShell
powershell -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"

# macOS / Linux
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Clone the repository and create the environment:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/holukas/ms-forests-vpd.git
cd ms-forests-vpd
uv sync --locked
```

`uv sync --locked` creates `.venv` from `uv.lock`, with every package at the locked
version. It downloads Python 3.12 if the system does not have it. With an empty uv cache,
a fresh install takes about three minutes on a standard desktop computer.

## Running scripts

Scripts import from `src/`, which `uv sync` installs in editable mode. Paths are resolved
from the repository root, so scripts run from any working directory:

```bash
uv run python scripts/30_shap/31_shap.py
```

## Packages

`pyproject.toml` pins the direct dependencies. `uv.lock` pins every package, including
the transitive ones. `pip install .` uses the direct pins only, not the lock file, so
transitive versions may differ. [Reproducibility](#reproducibility) describes how the
package versions affect the results.

| Package | Version | Used for |
|---------|---------|----------|
| `diive` | 0.91.1 | Parquet I/O, FLUXNET file reading, grid aggregation, heatmaps, ET from LE |
| `pandas` | 3.0.5 | Data handling |
| `numpy` | 2.4.6 | Numerics |
| `scipy` | 1.18.0 | Z-scores, nearest-neighbor search, statistics |
| `matplotlib` | 3.11.1 | Figures |
| `scikit-learn` | 1.9.0 | Cross-validation, metrics, hyperparameter search |
| `xgboost` | 3.0.5 | Gradient-boosted regression (the one pin that changes results) |
| `shap` | 0.52.0 | SHAP values via `TreeExplainer` |
| `pyale` | 1.2.0 | ALE curves |
| `statsmodels` | 0.14.6 | Spline row of the threshold robustness table |
| `geopandas` | 1.1.4 | Site map |
| `pyyaml` | 6.0.3 | Settings |
| `openpyxl` | 3.1.5 | Tables for Word |

## Demo

The data deposit (see [Data](data.qmd#deposited-outputs)) contains
`ms-forests-vpd_demo.zip` (10 MB) with the model input and the published model output of
one site, CH-Dav.

1. Create an empty data folder, point `MS_FORESTS_VPD_DATA` at it (see [Data](data.qmd)),
   and unpack the archive into `<data folder>/data/outputs/`.
2. Run `uv run python scripts/30_shap/31_shap.py`.

The script fits the XGBoost model of the site in five-fold cross-validation and computes
the out-of-sample SHAP values. This took 7 seconds on a 24-thread desktop computer. The
script writes `CH-Dav_shap-conditional_NEP_ZSCORE.parquet`, a run log and the
cross-validation results to `data/outputs/30_shap/NEP_ZSCORE/conditional/`. With xgboost
3.0.5 on 24 threads, the parquet file equals
`expected_output/CH-Dav_shap-conditional_NEP_ZSCORE.parquet` from the archive. With other
thread counts, the values differ by up to a few percent (see
[Reproducibility](#reproducibility)).

## Reproducibility

The published results were produced with xgboost 3.0.5 and `n_jobs=-1` on a 24-thread
machine. With that version and thread count, they reproduce bit for bit across all 208
sites. Both settings change the fitted trees through the order of floating-point
additions in the `hist` tree method:

- Under xgboost 3.3.0, predictions correlate at 0.995 with the published ones, the mean
  absolute SHAP of VPD is higher at every site tested, and the site-level VPD to soil
  moisture ratio is 6 to 21 percent higher. Out-of-sample R^2^ is unchanged.
- Under 3.0.5 with a different thread count, the early-stopping iteration at one site
  ranged from 478 (24 threads) to 1021 (one thread), and the site-level ratio from 1.53
  to 1.69.

These differences are per site. Aggregates over 208 sites are affected less.

The shap and scikit-learn versions make no difference. The results were produced with
shap 0.48.0 and scikit-learn 1.6.1, and the newer pinned versions, 0.52.0 and 1.9.0,
reproduce them exactly.

## Optional groups

```bash
uv sync --extra era5     # scripts 16a to 16d, ERA5 downloads, need credentials
uv sync --group dev      # JupyterLab, pytest, Quarto, ghp-import
```

## Building the documentation

The site is a [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) website under `docs/`. Nothing is executed at
render time, so no data folder is needed.

```powershell
.\preview_docs.ps1            # live preview
.\preview_docs.ps1 -Render    # build into docs/_site/
```

On other systems, run `uv run quarto preview docs` and `uv run quarto render docs`.
GitHub Actions builds the published site on every push to `main`.
